Write the general term $T_{r+1}$ in the binomial expansion of $\left(2x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^5$:
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{5}{r}(2x)^{5-r}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)^r = \binom{5}{r}2^{5-r}(-1)^r x^{5-2r}$$

To find the term in $x = x^1$, set the exponent of $x$ equal to $1$:
$$5 - 2r = 1 \implies 2r = 4 \implies r = 2$$

Evaluate the coefficient for $r = 2$:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x = \binom{5}{2}2^{5-2}(-1)^2 = 10 \times 8 \times 1 = 80$$

In the expansion of $(1 + 3x^2)\left(2x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^5$, the $x$ term arises from:
$$1 \times (\text{term in } x) + 3x^2 \times \left(\text{term in } \frac{1}{x}\right)$$

Find the term in $\frac{1}{x} = x^{-1}$ in $\left(2x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^5$:
$$5 - 2r = -1 \implies 2r = 6 \implies r = 3$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } \frac{1}{x} = \binom{5}{3}2^{5-3}(-1)^3 = 10 \times 4 \times (-1) = -40$$

Combine the two contributions:
$$\text{Total Coefficient of } x = 1(80) + 3(-40) = 80 - 120 = -40$$
